chapter: Los Angeles: Chico Hamilton, Webster, Giuffre
title: Joining the Chico Hamilton Quintet
summary: The quintet's personnel, the long run at The Strollers in Long Beach, and what the job meant to him.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Let’s talk a little bit about that quintet, because historically it was very innovative and unique and…
I don’t want to lead you on this.
I would really just like to know what your experience was with that. Did it click right away? Was it…? How, how did it [go?]?

Yeah, it was… Well, first of all, it literally was… I won’t say a lifesaver but I needed a job. (laughs) And I could, with my background I could, it would… Fred Katz played cello and piano. And then Buddy Collette played the woodwinds — clarinet and alto, and I don’t know if he played tenor. Carson Smith was the bass player, and Chico and me, I guess that’s it. The quintet. So it was a perfect job for me and we played at this club in Long Beach — The Strollers — for months. So I could write for the group and I did some of that and, so it… and my playing was getting better all the time. So that, that was, that was a perfect… And then, through Chico when we traveled back to New York, that’s when I met Sonny Rollins and all those people so…
We stick to the Chico group just for a minute.
I gotta grab my coffee. Is, is there a coffee?
Oh, there it is. Sorry. Male: (inaudible)
That’s okay, don’t worry. Sorry, Deb.
That’s okay. Kimery: (inaudible) when I was gonna do that, I was gonna shake this up just a tad there.
Oh, oh. Kimery: There we go.
I shouldn’t put coffee on it. (laughs)
